item.title: Iwami Ginzan: A World Heritage Silver Mine and Its Town — Guide
item.description: Iwami Ginzan was one of the most productive silver mines in the world: at its 16th–17th century peak it is said to have supplied as much as a third of the world’s silver, and it was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2007 — notably for having been worked sustainably, in harmony with its forested landscape, rather than through destructive large-scale extraction. Visitors can walk into the Ryugenji Mabu, one of hundreds of hand-dug tunnels, and then explore Omori, the exquisitely preserved former mining town of wooden merchant houses, temples and shops strung along a single quiet valley street.
